summary: src/router/ is one Node process-level proxy with three carrier lanes (HTTP by Host with WebSocket passthrough; Postgres wire on 5432 answering SSLRequest and terminating TLS to read SNI; TLS-SNI lanes for redis/mongo; plain per-port lanes for MySQL and for every database in local mode), one routing brain (a table rebuilt from state.json whenever State.rev changes), one hold-and-wake singleflight per service key `${branchId}:${serviceId}` that delegates the actual start to the scheduler's `wake()` and then port/wire-probes readiness, and one activity stamp writer (request start + 5 s ticker on the HTTP lane including upgraded sockets; every non-empty read on TCP lanes). Hostnames are `<group>-<ref>`, `pg-<ref>`, `<type>-<name>-<ref>` under INSTA_OSS_DOMAIN (server) or `.localhost` on the single 127.0.0.1:8080 listener (local, which also fronts the API via Fastify serverFactory so today's `http://127.0.0.1:8080` UX is unchanged). Apps reach their databases through the router in both modes via `--add-host <minted host>:host-gateway` injected on every compute container (a network_mode host container cannot join bridge networks, so the spec's alias idea is replaced; in local mode the DB host is 127.0.0.1:<lanePort> rewritten to host.docker.internal only inside the container env). Upstream discovery is `docker inspect` IP on the branch network in server mode and `docker port` (loopback-published ports) in local mode. Compute drops `-p` in server mode; Postgres/managed get `-p 127.0.0.1::<port>` in local mode only. The edge's `ask` is a loopback-only listener (127.0.0.1:8079), never a public route. Custom domains implement the cloud's four hidden `/projects/:id/compute/domain[s]` routes with ComputeDomainResult shapes. `GET /services/:sid/credentials` (cloud server.ts:2352) is added because `insta db url|connect` reads DATABASE_URL from it. No new dependency.

NEW, pure, no I/O. `hostFor(kind, ref, name, domain)` mints labels: compute `${group}-${ref}`, postgres `pg-${ref}`, managed `${type}-${name}-${ref}` (type = redis|mysql|mongodb, matching the CLI's service type). `buildTable(state, cfg): RouteTable` walks every branch: one Route per compute group with an app record, one per branch postgres, one per managed service; adds static routes `api.<domain>`/`console.<domain>` (kind 'api'), `s3.<domain>` and `*.s3.<domain>` (kind 'garage', upstream 127.0.0.1:3900 in server mode) and every `state.customDomains` entry as an alias of its compute route. Lookups: `byHost(host)`, `byPort(listenPort)`, `hosts(): Set<string>` (for ask). `hostOnly(hostHeader)` (strip :port, lowercase, strip trailing dot, validate labels <=63, total <=253, else '').

NEW `Router` class: constructor(deps: RouterDeps) where RouterDeps = { cfg; table(): RouteTable (mtime/rev cached); upstream(route): Promise<{host,port}|null>; intent(route): 'running'|'stopped'|'suspended'; wake(route): Promise<void>; touch(key): void; apiHandler(req,res): void }. `httpServer` (node:http via Fastify serverFactory), `start()` binds lanes per mode, `stop()`. NEW HTTP lane: request handler + 'upgrade' handler; hold-and-wake; reverse proxy over node:http.request with streaming; X-Forwarded-*; hop-by-hop header stripping; post-wake readiness retry (idempotent bodiless GET/HEAD/OPTIONS retried on 502/503/504 within READY_WINDOW; bodied requests gated by a HEAD probe then forwarded once); activity ticker.

NEW Postgres lane: first-packet classifier (SSLRequest 80877103, GSSENCRequest 80877104, StartupMessage 3.0, direct TLS ClientHello 0x16), 'S'/'N' answers, TLS termination with SNICallback, route by SNI (server) or listen port (local), wake, pg wire readiness probe, splice.

NEW `splice(a: net.Socket, b: net.Socket, opts: { idleMs; onBytes(): void })`: copies both directions with per-socket read timers, touch on every non-empty chunk, half-close (end) propagation, 2 s drain after the first side ends, idle cut when neither direction moved for idleMs. Port of insta-compute tcp.go splice (tcp.go:416-460).

NEW `awaitWake(key, run: () => Promise<void>, timeoutMs)` singleflight (Map<key, Promise>), `probePort(host, port, windowMs, stepMs=100, dialTimeout=500)` (port of router.go probeUpstream 1162-1185), `probePg(host, port, windowMs)` wire probe, `probeRedis(host, port, windowMs)`.

NEW discovery per mode: server → `docker inspect -f '{{(index .NetworkSettings.Networks "<net>").IPAddress}}' <container>` (empty = not running → null); local → `docker port <container> <port>/tcp` → '127.0.0.1:NNNN' (error = not running → null). LRU-less Map cache per container; `forget(container)` on ECONNREFUSED/EHOSTUNREACH/ETIMEDOUT and after every wake.

NEW `certFor(host)`: server mode looks in INSTA_OSS_TLS_CERT_DIR for `<host>.crt`+`<host>.key` at any depth (walk cached 60 s, exact hostname match, `*.` wildcard files honoured); falls back to `<DATA_DIR>/tls/self-signed.{crt,key}` generated once at start with `openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -nodes -subj /CN=<domain> -addext subjectAltName=DNS:<domain>,DNS:*.<domain> -days 3650` (openssl ships in the image; absent → TLS lanes disabled with a logged warning). algorithm:
## 0. Modes, listeners, ports (src/main.ts + src/router/index.ts)
local: one node:http server on INSTA_OSS_BIND(127.0.0.1):INSTA_OSS_PORT(8080) created by the router and handed to Fastify through `Fastify({ serverFactory: (handler) => { router.attach(handler); return router.httpServer } })`; on Linux the same server ALSO listens on the docker bridge gateway IP (`docker network inspect bridge -f '{{(index .IPAM.Config 0).Gateway}}'`, typically 172.17.0.1) so containers reach it through `--add-host …:host-gateway`; per-port DB lanes bind the same two addresses. No TLS, no internal listener, no SNI lanes.
server: HTTP server on 127.0.0.1:8080 (edge is the only client); internal listener 127.0.0.1:8079 (ask, healthz); pg lane 0.0.0.0:5432; redis SNI lane 0.0.0.0:6379; mongo SNI lane 0.0.0.0:27017; one plaintext port lane per MySQL service on 0.0.0.0:<lanePort>. TLS contexts from certs.ts. Startup order: load cfg → self-signed cert ensure → Fastify ready → `app.listen` (binds the shared server) → `router.start()` binds lanes; a lane port already in use aborts startup with the port named (the installer refuses busy 80/443/5432 for the same reason).
The routing table: `table()` = `if (cachedRev === loadState().rev) return cached; rebuild`. loadState is one JSON parse of a small file; the router additionally short-circuits with `statSync(statePath()).mtimeMs` before parsing. `router.invalidate()` clears the cache.

## 1. Hostnames (table.ts hostFor)
ref = engine.ref (frozen `<projectSlug>-<branchSlug>`, engine.ts:45-48). Labels: compute `${group}-${ref}` ('default' stays literal: `default-shop-main`); postgres `pg-${ref}`; managed `${type}-${name}-${ref}` (redis-cache-shop-main, mysql-x-…, mongodb-y-…). FQDN = `${label}.${cfg.domain}` (local: `web-shop-main.localhost`). Static: `api.${domain}`, `console.${domain}`, `s3.${domain}`, `*.s3.${domain}`. Reserved: no minted label may equal `api|console|s3`; every minted label is validated `^[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?$` and must be absent from `buildTable(state).hosts()` at the time the engine mints it (branch create checks every label the new branch will mint; service add checks the label on every existing branch). URLs: server `https://<fqdn>`; local `http://<fqdn>:${cfg.port}`. Lane addresses: postgres server `pg-<ref>.<domain>:5432` tls; local `127.0.0.1:<branch.lanes['pg-db']>` plain; redis/mongo server `<label>.<domain>:6379|27017` tls; mysql server `<label>.<domain>:<branch.lanes[id]>` plain; all managed local `127.0.0.1:<branch.lanes[id]>` plain. Minted URL forms: DATABASE_URL server `postgres://postgres:<pw>@pg-<ref>.<domain>:5432/app?sslmode=require`, local `postgres://postgres:<pw>@127.0.0.1:<port>/app`; redis server `rediss://default:<pw>@<host>:6379/0`; mongo server `…?authSource=admin&tls=true`. In the compute container env only (deployLocked → containerize()), local-mode URLs have host 127.0.0.1 rewritten to `host.docker.internal`; server-mode env is byte-identical to what `/secrets` returns (ONE URL). Every compute container in both modes gets `--add-host <fqdn>:host-gateway` for each host minted on its branch (its own, siblings, pg, managed) plus `--add-host host.docker.internal:host-gateway` (a no-op on Docker Desktop, required on Linux). Rationale per mode: server = daemon is a network_mode host container, which Docker forbids from joining bridge networks, so the spec's per-network alias is impossible; host-gateway is a host address reachable from any bridge network without depending on public-DNS hairpin (an elastic IP not on the interface would break hairpin). local = the daemon is a host process on macOS/Linux; it cannot join docker networks at all and Docker Desktop cannot route host→container IPs, so the only host→container path is a loopback-published port and the only container→host path is host.docker.internal/host-gateway; `*.localhost` does not resolve for non-browser clients on macOS, hence 127.0.0.1 in the host-facing DSN.

## 2. Table build (buildTable)
For each branch b of project p: ref = b.ref ?? `${p.refSlug ?? slug(p.name)}-${slug(b.name)}`; net = b.network; routes:
- for each [group, app] in b.apps: { key: `${b.id}:cp-${group}`, host: `${group}-${ref}.${domain}`, aliases: customDomains where branchId===b.id && group===group, kind:'compute', lane:'http', container:`io-${ref}-app-${group}`, network: net, port: app.port, tls:false }.
- postgres: { key: `${b.id}:pg-db`, host:`pg-${ref}.${domain}`, kind:'postgres', lane:'pg', container:`io-${ref}-pg`, port:5432, listenPort: mode==='local' ? b.lanes?.['pg-db'] : cfg.lanePgPort, tls: mode==='server' }.
- for each m in p.managedServices with b.managed?.[m.id]: container = managedContainerName(ref, m.type, m.name); lane = mode==='server' && MANAGED_DB[m.type].sni ? 'sni' : 'port'; listenPort = lane==='sni' ? (redis 6379 | mongo 27017) : b.lanes?.[m.id]; tls = lane==='sni'.
Index: byHost (host + aliases, lowercased), byPort (lane==='port' routes and local-mode pg), hosts(). Duplicate host → throw (engine guards prevent it).

## 3. HTTP lane (http.ts)
On `request` (and `upgrade`, same steps 1-6 then §3b):
1. host = hostOnly(req.headers.host). tlsOrigin = (server mode && req.socket.remoteAddress is loopback && x-forwarded-proto === 'https').
2. Dispatch: server mode: host ∈ {api.<domain>, console.<domain>} → deps.apiHandler(req,res) and return; local mode: if host is 'localhost', an IP literal, empty, or not ending in `.localhost` → apiHandler; else continue. (`api.<domain>` and console get no stamps.)
3. route = table.byHost(host). None → 404 JSON {error:'unknown route'}. Garage kind → proxy to 127.0.0.1:3900 (no wake, no stamp). kind !== 'compute' → 503 {error:'this service serves no HTTP endpoint'}.
4. intent = deps.intent(route): 'stopped' → 503 {error:'service is stopped'}; 'suspended' → 503 {error:'service is suspended'}. Traffic never overrides explicit user intent (sleep-and-wake.md 1.5: stopped is never woken by traffic).
5. deps.touch(route.key); start ticker = setInterval(() => deps.touch(route.key), TOUCH_DEBOUNCE_MS); cleared on res 'close' (or upgraded socket 'close'). This is the cloud's HTTP rule (sleep-and-wake.md 1.2: request start then every 5 s while the handler runs; an open WebSocket holds by time).
6. up = await deps.upstream(route). If null (container not running): woke = true; `await awaitWake(route.key, () => deps.wake(route), WAKE_TIMEOUT_MS)` — singleflight: Map<key, Promise>; first caller creates the promise `deps.wake(route).then(()=>upstreamCache.forget(route.container))` with a timeout race; later callers await the same promise; entry deleted in finally. Errors: timeout → 504 {error:'service wake timed out'}; WakeRefused → 503 with its reason; other → 503 {error:'service could not be woken'}; client aborted (req 'close' before wake) → stop waiting, nothing written. After wake: up = await deps.upstream(route); null → 503 'service could not be woken'. Then `await probePort(up.host, up.port, PROBE_WINDOW_MS)` (dial every 100 ms, 500 ms dial timeout; failure → 502 {error:'upstream not accepting'} and forget cache).
7. Proxy: outbound headers = req.headers minus hop-by-hop (connection, keep-alive, proxy-authenticate, proxy-authorization, te, trailer, transfer-encoding, upgrade; plus any header named in `connection`), with `host` kept as the client sent it (customer-facing Host, router.go:417-446), `x-forwarded-for` appended with req.socket.remoteAddress, `x-forwarded-proto` = tlsOrigin ? 'https' : (existing value from loopback only, else 'http'), `x-forwarded-host` = host. `const out = http.request({ host: up.host, port: up.port, method, path: req.url, headers, setHost: false, agent: keepAliveAgent(maxSockets 256) })`; `req.pipe(out)`; on 'response' r: copy status + headers (drop hop-by-hop), `r.pipe(res)`; on out 'error' → if !res.headersSent: 502 {error:'upstream unreachable'}; forget cache on ECONNREFUSED/EHOSTUNREACH/ETIMEDOUT; else destroy res. No response timeout (SSE/long polls). `server.requestTimeout = 0; server.headersTimeout = 60000; server.keepAliveTimeout = 65000`.
8. Post-wake readiness retry (only when woke): if method ∈ {GET, HEAD, OPTIONS} and no body (no content-length/transfer-encoding): run the attempt against a holdback: if upstream status ∈ {502,503,504} and Date.now()+backoff < deadline (READY_WINDOW_MS from wake completion): drain up to 64 KiB / 1 s then retry after backoff (200 ms doubling to 1 s, ±25% jitter); otherwise commit (on give-up commit the last held answer verbatim). Any other status commits and streams immediately (nothing buffered on the happy path). Bodied or non-idempotent requests: before forwarding once, loop `HEAD /` (client's headers) until a non-{502,503,504} status or the deadline, then forward exactly once.
3b. Upgrade (WebSocket etc.): after step 6, `const up = net.connect(port, host)`; on connect write `${req.method} ${req.url} HTTP/1.1\r\n` + headers (outbound set from step 7 INCLUDING `connection: Upgrade` and `upgrade` and `sec-websocket-*`) + `\r\n` + head buffer; then `splice(socket, up, { idleMs: 0 /* no idle cut for websockets */, onBytes: noop })` while the ticker from step 5 keeps stamping until either socket closes (time-held, cloud parity). Connect error → write `HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway\r\n\r\n` and destroy.

## 4. Postgres lane (pg.ts)
Listener: server mode `net.createServer` on LANE_BIND:5432; local mode one `net.createServer` per pg route on 127.0.0.1(+bridge gateway):<listenPort> from table.byPort (listeners reconciled against the table on every `table()` rebuild: add missing, close removed).
Per connection c:
1. Read the first 8 bytes with a 10 s timeout (`c.once('readable')` loop; total buffer B). Classify by B: if B[0]===0x16 → direct TLS (PG17 sslnegotiation=direct); else len=B.readUInt32BE(0), code=B.readUInt32BE(4): code===80877103 → SSLRequest; code===80877104 → GSSENCRequest; (code>>>16)===3 → StartupMessage; else → destroy.
2. GSSENCRequest → write 'N', consume 8 bytes, go to 1 (libpq then sends SSLRequest or Startup).
3. SSLRequest: server mode → write 'S', consume 8 bytes, `tlsSock = new tls.TLSSocket(c, { isServer: true, SNICallback: (name, cb) => cb(null, certs.certFor(name) ?? certs.selfSigned()), secureContext: certs.selfSigned() })`; on 'secure': sni = hostOnly(tlsSock.servername ?? ''); route = table.byHost(sni); none or route.lane!=='pg' → send ErrorResponse over tlsSock (§4e, SQLSTATE 08P01, 'no database at this hostname (SNI)') and end. local mode → write 'N', consume 8, go to 1 (the client falls back to plaintext Startup; sslmode=prefer default), route = table.byPort(c.localPort).
4. StartupMessage as the FIRST packet: server mode → ErrorResponse 'SSL is required: add sslmode=require to your connection string' (08P01) then end; local mode → route = byPort, keep B as `pending` bytes to forward. Direct TLS → server mode: `c.unshift(B)` then the same TLSSocket wrap as step 3 (TLS handshake starts from the ClientHello); local mode → destroy.
5. intent: postgres has no user stop in v1 → always 'running'. deps.touch(route.key) once at connect.
6. up = await deps.upstream(route); null → awaitWake (same singleflight as §3, WAKE_TIMEOUT_MS); failure → ErrorResponse (57P03 'the database is waking up; retry' on timeout, 08P01 otherwise) and end. Then readiness `probePg(up, PROBE_WINDOW_MS + READY_WINDOW_MS)`: open a TCP connection, send SSLRequest, read 1 byte ('S' → destroy and retry with a plain probe is unnecessary: the official image answers 'N' by default; if 'S', wrap in tls with rejectUnauthorized:false), send StartupMessage {user:'postgres', database:'postgres'} (protocol 3.0), read the first message: 'R' (Authentication*) → ready; 'E' → parse fields, code 57P03 ('starting up') or 'C' 'the database system is starting up' → sleep 250 ms and retry; any other 'E' → ready (auth/other errors mean the server is up); connection refused → retry until window; window exceeded → ErrorResponse 57P03 and end. (Equivalent to pg_isready without a docker exec per 250 ms.)
7. `upSock = net.connect(up.port, up.host)`; on connect: if `pending` bytes exist write them; then `splice(clientSide /* tlsSock or c */, upSock, { idleMs: LANE_IDLE_MS, onBytes: () => deps.touch(route.key) })`. Note the client's SSLRequest never reaches upstream (consumed), so upstream sees a plaintext Startup; the router-to-container hop is plaintext on the branch network / loopback-published port, which is the cloud's model too (tcp.go:19-28: terminate, then plain TCP to the upstream).
4e. ErrorResponse encoding: 'E' + int32 len + fields 'S' 'FATAL' \0, 'V' 'FATAL' \0, 'C' <sqlstate> \0, 'M' <message> \0, \0. Written on the plaintext or TLS side matching where the client is.

## 5. SNI lanes (tls.ts, server mode only)
`tls.createServer({ SNICallback: (name, cb) => cb(null, certs.certFor(name) ?? certs.selfSigned()), minVersion: 'TLSv1.2' })` on LANE_BIND:6379 and :27017; on 'secureConnection' s: host = hostOnly(s.servername ?? ''); route = byHost(host); none / route.lane!=='sni' / route.port !== listener port's expected kind → s.destroy() (the cloud refuses at connection level, tcp.go:304-316). intent always 'running'. touch once. upstream/wake as §3 step 6; readiness: redis → open TCP, send `*1\r\n$4\r\nPING\r\n`, first byte '+' or '-' with 'NOAUTH'/'WRONGPASS' → ready, '-LOADING' → retry 250 ms, window PROBE+READY; mongo → probePort only. Then splice(s, upSock, { idleMs: LANE_IDLE_MS, onBytes: touch }).

## 6. Port lanes (port.ts)
One `net.createServer` per route with lane==='port' on `<bind>:<listenPort>` (local: every managed service and, via pg.ts, postgres; server: MySQL only). Reconciled with the table like §4. On connection: route = byPort(localPort); touch; upstream/wake; readiness = probePort (MySQL greets first, so the greeting flows through the splice; a client that sent bytes before the upstream was dialed has them buffered by `c.pause()` until connect, then `c.resume()`); splice with touch. Local-mode mysql/redis/mongo are plaintext; local-mode pg goes through pg.ts's 'N' path.

## 7. splice (splice.ts)
```
function splice(a, b, { idleMs, onBytes }) {
  let last = Date.now(); let ended = 0
  const pump = (src, dst) => {
    src.on('data', (chunk) => { if (chunk.length) { last = Date.now(); onBytes() } if (!dst.write(chunk)) { src.pause(); dst.once('drain', () => src.resume()) } })
    src.on('end', () => { dst.end(); if (++ended === 1) setTimeout(() => { a.destroy(); b.destroy() }, 2000).unref() })
    src.on('error', () => { a.destroy(); b.destroy() })
  }
  pump(a, b); pump(b, a)
  if (idleMs > 0) { const t = setInterval(() => { if (Date.now() - last >= idleMs) { a.destroy(); b.destroy() } }, Math.min(idleMs, 30000)); a.once('close', () => clearInterval(t)) }
}
```
Both raw lanes stamp per non-empty chunk in either direction (sleep-and-wake.md 1.2 TCP row); a silent open connection stamps nothing and is cut after LANE_IDLE_MS (15 min default, tcp.go:39-40).

## 8. Upstream discovery (upstream.ts)
`upstream(route)`: cache hit → return. server: `docker inspect -f '{{(index .NetworkSettings.Networks "${route.network}").IPAddress}}' ${route.container}` → '' or error → null; else {host: ip, port: route.port}. local: `docker port ${route.container} ${route.port}/tcp` → first line `127.0.0.1:NNNN` → {host:'127.0.0.1', port: NNNN}; error/empty → null (a created-but-not-started or exited container has no mapping). Cache Map<container, addr>; `forget(container)` on dial errors and after every completed wake (Desktop reassigns ephemeral ports on every start; Linux may reassign IPs). A stopped container that still has a cached address surfaces as ECONNREFUSED on dial → forget → the NEXT request takes the wake path; to avoid one failed request per sleep, the scheduler calls `router.forget(container)` when it stops a container (seam on Router: `forgetUpstream(container)`), and the HTTP lane treats a dial ECONNREFUSED on a cache hit as 'maybe asleep': forget, re-resolve, and if null go to the wake path within the same request (bounded to one retry).

## 9. Activity (activity.ts)
`touch(key)`: if now - map.get(key) < debounce → return; else map.set(key, now). `last(key)` → map.get(key) ?? startedAt. Map pruned of entries older than 24 h every 10 min. In-memory by design: stamps every 5 s per active service would otherwise rewrite state.json continuously; a daemon restart resets every stamp to 'now', which is the cloud's ready-stamp behaviour after a (re)deploy (sleep-and-wake.md 1.2 executor row) and gives one full window before any sleep.

## 10. Compute adapter (compute.ts)
`docker create --restart unless-stopped --name <n> --network <net> [-e …] [-v vol:/data] [--add-host h:host-gateway …] [-p 127.0.0.1:<hostPort>:<port> when opts.hostPort !== undefined] <image>`; start unless opts.start===false. The engine passes hostPort only in local mode (its allocator, engine.ts:263-289, is kept for local mode, now loopback-bound; server mode passes none, deleting the collision surface there). Postgres/managed provision add `-p 127.0.0.1::<port>` when publishLoopback (local mode) so `docker port` can find them.

## 11. Custom domains (domains.ts + server.ts)
normalizeHostname: trim, lowercase, strip trailing dot, punycode as given, validate (<=253, labels 1..63, `[a-z0-9-]`, no leading/trailing '-'), refuse hostnames ending in `.${cfg.domain}` or equal to it (400), refuse IP literals. set: resolve branch (body.branch ?? default) and group (body.group ?? sole compute group, else 400 'group required'); the group must have an app record on that branch (404 'no compute deployed'); if state.customDomains[h] exists for a different (branchId, group) → 409 { error: `${h} is already attached to <group>` }; same target → idempotent 200. Write entry; bump rev; router picks it up (alias on the compute route); the ask endpoint now answers 200 for it so the edge issues a certificate on first request. status derivation: dns = [{ type:'CNAME', name:h, value:`api.${domain}`, note: publicIp ? `or an A record to ${publicIp}` : undefined, status }] where status: `dns.promises.resolve4(h)` compared with resolve4(`api.${domain}`) (or publicIp) → 'ok' | mismatch/ENOTFOUND → 'pending' | other error → 'unchecked'; `status` = 'ready' when dns ok AND ssl issued, else 'pending'; `ssl` = certs.certFor(h) found in INSTA_OSS_TLS_CERT_DIR → 'issued' else 'pending'; configured: true; flyApp: `io-${ref}-app-${group}`; service: group; region: 'local'. list: entries filtered by project (and branch/group). remove: 404 when not bound in this project; delete entry. Teardown: destroyBranch/destroyProject/removeComputeService/renameComputeService(rename moves entries to the new group) call releaseDomainsFor before the container work, matching the cloud invariant that a hostname never outlives its service (custom-domains.ts:3-14). Gates: POST/DELETE gated 'deploy' (server.ts:2786, :2806); GETs ungated. Local mode: routes work identically (the router honours the alias by Host) but ssl is reported 'external'.

## 12. Internal listener (internal.ts, server mode)
node:http on 127.0.0.1:8079. `GET /ask?domain=X`: h = hostOnly(X); 200 'ok' if h ∈ table.hosts() (service hosts, custom domains, api., console., s3.) or h ends with `.s3.${domain}` and the label is an existing bucket (`io-<ref>`) ; else 404. `GET /healthz` → 200 {ok:true}. Everything else 404. Bound to loopback only; documented as the edge's on-demand-TLS check, not an API.

risks: Docker forbids a network_mode host container from joining bridge networks, so the spec's 'router joins every branch network with aliases' cannot be built as written; this design uses --add-host host-gateway instead. Verify on the target distro that containers on user-defined bridges reach the host's docker0 gateway address on 443/5432 (ufw/firewalld on some VPS images drop docker→host INPUT; the installer should add an allow rule for 172.16.0.0/12 → 443,5432,6379,27017 and the lane range).

Self-signed fallback on 5432/6379/27017: psql (sslmode=prefer/require) accepts it, but node-postgres with `?sslmode=require` verifies the chain and will fail until the edge has issued a real certificate; docs must say to use `sslmode=no-verify` in that window. Redis clients do not all send SNI (redis-cli needs --sni or a hostname-aware build); mongo drivers do.

Local mode: `*.localhost` URLs work in browsers (Chrome/Firefox resolve them to loopback) and on Linux (nss-myhostname) but not for curl/psql on macOS; that is why the host-facing DSN is 127.0.0.1:<port> and why `endpoint` keeps `localhost:<hostPort>`. Two textual forms of the local DSN (127.0.0.1 outside, host.docker.internal inside) is a deliberate local-only deviation; server mode has exactly one.

Docker Desktop reassigns the ephemeral loopback port of `-p 127.0.0.1::5432` on every docker start, so the local-mode upstream cache must be dropped after every wake (designed) and a stale entry costs one ECONNREFUSED retry.

Hostname collisions: `<group>-<projectSlug>-<branch>` is a flat label, so project `shop`+branch `main-main` and project `shop-main`+branch `main` mint the same host; the engine-level assertHostFree/ref-exists checks close this, but older state created before the check may already collide (startup logs duplicates and skips the later branch).

Cloud lists /compute/domain* as hidden routes (schema: { hide: true }); if the platform team changes ComputeDomainResult, the CLI renderer is the contract we mirror (compute.ts:54-62), not openapi.yaml.

Activity stamps are in memory: a daemon restart gives every service one full idle window before it can sleep (accepted, mirrors the cloud's ready stamp) and a crash mid-window can sleep a service the user was about to hit (bounded by the window).

Fastify serverFactory: Fastify registers its request listener on the provided server; the router must be the ONLY 'request' listener and must call Fastify's handler itself, and 'upgrade' has no Fastify listener, so ordering is safe; but @fastify/static's sendFile path and Fastify's own error handler still run inside the shared server, so an API-path exception cannot take down lane sockets (they are separate servers).
The post-wake HEAD gating for bodied requests can double an app's side effects only if its HEAD handler has side effects (rare); the cloud accepted the same trade (#197).
openQuestions: Default compute group label: literal `default-<ref>` (unambiguous, chosen here) vs bare `<ref>` for the 'default' group (prettier, needs an extra reserved-label rule). Tony's URL-shape sign-off (spec action item 1) should settle it.

Should database sleep also honour a user 'stop' in v1? The cloud gates always-on for managed DBs (server.ts:2167) but oss has no stop verb for pg-db; this design treats all database intents as 'running' so traffic always wakes them.

Certificate store layout of the chosen edge (file naming under INSTA_OSS_TLS_CERT_DIR) is WP0's pick; certs.ts scans for `<host>.crt/.key` at any depth and needs the real layout confirmed (or a small converter in the installer).
MySQL external port in server mode: dedicated port from INSTA_OSS_LANE_PORT_RANGE (chosen) vs in-network only. Ports in the range must be opened by the installer's firewall step.
Whether the scheduler wants the router to expose `forgetUpstream(container)` (chosen) or prefers the router to poll docker state; the former is cheaper and is what this design assumes.
Local mode HTTP listener also binding the docker bridge gateway IP on Linux is needed for in-container `${services.x.url}` self-calls; confirm this is acceptable versus exposing 8080 on 0.0.0.0.
dependsOn: WP0 packaging/identity: cfg.mode/domain/dataDir come from the installer's env; the edge's upstream (127.0.0.1:8080), ask URL (127.0.0.1:8079/ask) and cert-store mount are installer-owned; auth must whitelist nothing for the router (no Fastify routes added by WP2 besides compute/domain* and credentials, which need the WP0 bearer/session check like every other route).

WP3 scheduler: implements engine.wakeService (memory floor, eviction, docker start, running wait, WakeRefused for stopped/suspended) and stop-with-grace; reads activity.last(key) with the `${branchId}:${serviceId}` key; calls router.forgetUpstream(container) after a stop.
WP4 data dir/branching: bind-mount changes to postgres/manageddb provision must keep the publishLoopback flag and container names; volume forks do not affect routing.

WP5 templates/project parity: `${services.<name>.url}` resolves to apps[group].url minted here; multiple postgres/storage per project would extend hostFor (a second postgres needs `pg-<name>-<ref>`, reserved by this design's assertHostFree but not minted yet).
Garage WP: `s3.<domain>` root_domain and the 127.0.0.1:3900 host port in server mode; presigned URLs must use `https://s3.<domain>` so they pass through the edge → router garage route.
